value.body: A music producer turns musical ideas into finished tracks. They arrange songs, program instruments, record singers and players, and edit and mix the result. Work comes from independent artists, music labels, film and ad projects, games and online creators.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Music training (BPA, B.Mus. or similar) plus a course or self-learning in audio production

items.label: Common tools
items.value: A digital audio workstation (DAW), MIDI keyboard, microphones, plugins

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Learn a DAW, build a portfolio of tracks and work as an assistant in a studio or with an established producer or composer. Small paid projects for independent artists and creators often come first.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Working to a client brief and deadline

value.title: At a glance
items: Most producers work freelance or in small studios.
A body of released work matters more than a degree for most clients.
Related paths include sound engineering, composing and audio post-production.
